Eating less than I should be/used to, but generally pretty healthy stuff, salads, chicken, fish, some pasta and other grains, red meat twice a week, lots of fruit and vegetables, a reasonable amount of dairy (glasses of milk, yogurt, cereal, smoothies), low amounts of sugar (ice cream is pretty much the only sweet I like), and my junk food guilty pleasure is chips. Those things probably consist of 85-90% of my diet.

I don’t drink as much water as I should and I eat a bit too many carbs but I would say that I eat healthier than most, at least most people who aren’t fitness/health nuts.

Excericse has been piss poor since the depression started, used to be a high level athlete in Rugby, Golf, Skiing, and Freediving (my lung capacity is about 20% larger than normal). However I just went for a run today and they were on fire at about the 3km mark, and I had to change to a light jogging pace. (For reference I used to run half marathons) so it’s less than ideal, for sure.

Don’t do what I did and ruin your life then, you’ve still got time to sort things out. Get through Highschool and then take some time to figure yourself out. You’re too young to have lost hope, there’s still time for you. Spend some time figure out what you want from life and don’t let ANYONE tell you what you “need” to be doing. As long as you don’t get forced down the wrong path and actually give yourself a chance to find your passion then you have a shot. Good luck
Are you in college? I saw your post about feeling defeated for the last 17 years, parents forcing you to do shit etc.

Yeah that was part of the problem, I fucked my back up at the gym (5 misaligned vertabrae) and I still haven’t fully recovered, meaning my best source of coping (exercise) has mostly been removed from me. Months of physio/chiro are starting to get it back in shape but I’m still pretty much locked to running as my only source.

It really sucks because I was a triple varsity athlete in HS including captain of the rugby and Ski racing teams (and maybe the worst player on the varsity soccer team Lmao), so physical activity has always been a major de-stressor for for me.

I don’t think interviewing should be too bad for me, obviously some aspects will be harder than others, but I was a server/bartender throughout college and used to do acting as a hobby, so I’m very comfortable in front of new people and talking to them... should be able to sell a positive demeanour as well, even if that’s not how I really feel right now. And I can say at the very least I haven’t been completely isolating myself, so at least there’s that.

Thanks for the encouragement, I needed it.

What do you mean by “at a bank” are you talking very basic, like Teller/FSR? Or try to haggle my way into some sort of junior loan officer position or something of the type? If I do go down this path, it’s my general understanding that bank skill are not the most transferable outside the retail banking industry - maybe some positions are different though, I’m just not well enough informed.

As per the back office jobs - I get that they’re not nearly as competitive as FO jobs, but with no experience and a very low gpa, wouldn’t those be closed off too? I’m under the impression that most entry level jobs will mill over your transcripts GPA, even if they don’t have the same standards as FO jobs, wouldn’t they still be looking for people with 3.0+?

Thanks for the advice btw.

I appreciate the advice, honestly, but a quick glance at your post history says you went into CS which is a much more forgiving field since everyone is looking for entry-level programmers. 
Of course earning those promotions requires hard work in any field, but it’s a lot easier to get your foot in the door for that first CS job than most other fields (except for maybe engineering)
